questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nice sized European city. A city with both a good university and a great student life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A little bit hard. It was not always very structured but everyone is very forgiving.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. Sadly there is only a introduction programme for some degrees. Economics does not have. Law does.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I used
Uniplaces.com
. They are legit when the renter is "verified". A lot of people use a guy on WhatsApp named Laif. And a lot of people connected with other students seeking room mates on Facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is no on campus living. I will recommend living inside the city walls.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is a bit expensive. But comparing to Copenhagen most people should then manage. I would try to find housing early but a lot of people found housing only weeks before the start.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of stuff can be quite unclear.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to join a Microsoft Teams queue and show your passport and so on. It is quite fast to do.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They can be helpful on their virtual help desk but not too much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. It is quite easy to opt in and out of classes that you see fit. Some classes require attendance.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start only but do not stress. They are quite large and most errors can be fixed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels of the course vary a lot. Most of the time it was quite easy. I had on course that was hard and fit the level of UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes are often quite small so you get more contact with the instructor. Some of the exam grading can be very different, so look out for that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
B2018 NEGOTIATION AND BARGAINING
B2035 ENVIRONMENTAL ECONOMIC POLICY
90350 Causal Inference And Program Evaluation
B2023 R FOR ECONOMISTS
91681 Internship I

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
B2018 NEGOTIATION AND BARGAINING
Was a very nice course. It was very fun and a very different type of teaching. Every class was very practical and it was therefore quite refreshing to have if you are used to a lot of lectures.

90350 Causal Inference And Program Evaluation
Is pretty much the same as UCPH's Applied Econometric Policy Evaluation. It is quite hard but you learn a lot of great econometric methods and theory.

B2023 R FOR ECONOMISTS
Nice for a very beginner friendly introduction to R.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None. Bologna is not as cheap as I had hoped.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks are more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not really aware of any non-academic opportunities. I did not mind though.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I know there were some sport clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Eat a lot of great food and take the trains to a lot of different cities and areas. Try to explore. Never stay at home.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Bologna is great for hiking. Otherwise I would recommend doing as many one-day or weekend trips to nearby cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is quite easy if you know how Italians behave. But they are not very strict. Remember to always take the receipt when they offer you it. They can get pissed about it as it is Italian law that the costumer has to get it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are very open and talkative. They love the Nordics. Try just to ask them if they want a coffee or a drink.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found that the local students are a bit younger. I could feel the difference. Bologna is a quite progressive city but you can still feel the different values between Danish and Italians.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the going out culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Relax. Dont stress about all the administrative stuff. It will work out. Italians dont stress.
Explore. Dont sit at home in your appartement. Explore the city and its surroundings. Explore Italy.
Try to meet a lot of people at the start and then invest as much time as possible in those you like. You will not have time to be friends with everyone.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The Irish Pub Cluricane hosts all Erasmus students every Tuesday. Go there the first few Tuesdays. It can really help you find some friends.
After that go to the better bars on for example Aldrovandi and Pratello.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I got and the time away from my everyday life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not feeling you are wasting your exchange by not doing anything.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Bologna is a great city. I think it is one of the best places to go to exchange. It is a very young and lively city.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
